Brzesko Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Brzesko, Poland

Demolished. Brzesko's Jewish population reached 1,935 (61.5 percent of the town) by 1921, most later killed by the Germans at Bełżec in 1942. This, the older of Brzesko's two Jewish cemeteries, was likely established in the 17th century; in 1787, the town's owner, Count Kryspin Żeleński, sought to close it to make way for city expansion, but protests from Brzesko's Jews led Lviv Governorate authorities to block the closure. The cemetery nonetheless closed in the 1820s-30s due to overcrowding, when a new burial ground was established. During the Polish People's Republic era, a car park was built on the site; a tombstone-styled commemorative monument was unveiled there on October 7, 2018.
